result.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema is only z.array(z.string().email()) while the client-side copy adds a uniqueness refine. The handler's uniqueGuests filter checks guests against booking.attendees but not for duplicates within the input array itself, so a direct API mutation with duplicate emails would create duplicate attendee records (createMany with the same email twice) — a real correctness gap, not merely stylistic duplication.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate validation definitions with different semantics: the client-side `AddGuestsDialog` defines a local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness, while the server-side shared input schema `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` without uniqueness. This duplicates/fragmentates validation logic across files and allows the server route to accept duplicate emails even though the UI rejects them, creating inconsistent behavior.
